title: Martial arts of South and Southeast Asia
blurb: Empty hand, stick, blade and rope, taught in a kalari, a village square or a temple courtyard: Kerala's gymnasiums, the Philippine stick schools, the ring sports of Thailand and Myanmar.

items.s: Kalaripayattu (Malayalam: [kɐɭɐɾipːɐjɐtːɨ̆]), also known simply as Kalari, is an Indian martial art that originated in modern-day Kerala during the 11th–12th centuries CE.
Silambam is an old Indian martial art originating in the southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu.
Thang Ta (/thaang-taa/) is a classical Meitei traditional martial art form.
Malla-yuddha (Sanskrit: मल्लयुद्ध, IAST: mallayuddha) is the traditional form of combat-wrestling originating in the Indian subcontinent.
Pehlwani, also known as Kushti, is a style of grappling and wrestling.

Lathi khela (Bengali: লাঠি খেলা) is a traditional Bengali martial art – a kind of stick fighting practiced in India and Bangladesh.
Varma Kalai (Tamil: வர்மக்கலை, varmakalai), also known as Marma Vidhya ( Sanskrit: marma-vidya/marmam) is an Indian traditional art of pressure points.
Pencak silat (Indonesian pronunciation: [ˈpənt͡ʃaʔ ˈsilat]; in Western writings sometimes spelled "pentjak silat" or phonetically as "penchak silat") is a class of related Indonesian martial arts.
Arnis, also known as eskrima/escrima or kali, is the national martial art of the Philippines.

Krabi-Krabong (Thai: กระบี่กระบอง, pronounced [krā.bìː krā.bɔ̄ːŋ]) is a weapon-based martial art from Thailand.

Bando (Burmese: ဗန်တို, pronounced [bàɰ̃dò]) is a defensive unarmed martial art from Myanmar.
